items.stem: What is meant by "Simple cash book"?
items.answer: A cash book with only one amount column on each side, recording cash transactions only.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A cash book with only one amount column on each side, recording cash transactions only.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the simple cash book is correct?
items.answer: Credit transactions are not recorded in the cash book.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Credit transactions are not recorded in the cash book.
options: Credit purchases are recorded on the credit side of the cash book.
The cash book can have a credit balance.
Credit transactions are not recorded in the cash book.
Payments are recorded on the debit side of the cash book.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A simple cash book can never show a credit balance.
Reason (R): Cash payments cannot exceed cash receipts plus the opening balance.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true and R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Distinguish between debit note and credit note on the basis of sent to, account affected in the sender's books, prepared by and occasion.
items.answer: (i) Sent to: debit note: the supplier; credit note: the customer. (ii) Account affected in the sender's books: debit note: the supplier's account is debited; credit note: the customer's account is credited. (iii) Prepared by: debit note: the buyer (purchaser); credit note: the seller. (iv) Occasion: debit note: goods returned to the supplier (purchases return); credit note: goods returned by the customer (sales return).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Sent to: debit note: the supplier; credit note: the customer. (ii) Account affected in the sender's books: debit note: the supplier's account is debited; credit note: the customer's account is credited. (iii) Prepared by: debit note: the buyer (purchaser); credit note: the seller. (iv) Occasion: debit note: goods returned to the supplier (purchases return); credit note: goods returned by the customer (sales return).

(4) Paid ₹4,000 in cash as donation to a relief fund. (5) Purchased goods with a list price of ₹46,000 from Mishra Enterprises on credit at 10% trade discount. (6) Received commission ₹16,800. (7) Received ₹24,950 in cash from Kunal in full settlement of ₹25,500.
items.answer: Closing balance ₹79,250; items (2), (5) are not entered
items.markingKey: Items (2), (5) involve no cash and go to other books. Receipts ₹69,750, payments ₹24,000; balance = ₹33,500 + ₹69,750 − ₹24,000 = ₹79,250.
